supportingEvidence.title: Kioxia and Sandisk to invest over $31 billion in Japan
supportingEvidence.note: Primary joint announcement says the companies anticipate more than $31B (about 5 trillion yen) of investment in Japan through 2032, contingent on government support, to expand Yokkaichi/Kitakami infrastructure and support strong AI/data-driven demand for flash memory.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Kioxia and Sandisk plan more than $31B Japan investment amid AI boom
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters independently reports the same investment scale and government-support dependency, tying it to rising AI-related memory demand.

supportingEvidence.title: Sandisk: 10th-generation 3D flash production already underway at Kitakami
supportingEvidence.note: Earlier primary evidence confirms the partners are already scaling advanced flash production at Kitakami, so the new plan extends an operating manufacturing base rather than describing a greenfield concept only.

contradictingEvidence.title: Investment remains contingent and long-dated
contradictingEvidence.note: The companies explicitly condition the plan on government support and spread investment through 2032. Announced capital does not equal completed fabs, delivered bit growth, utilization, pricing power, or attractive returns.

falsifier: Downgrade the thesis if government support is materially reduced, planned Yokkaichi/Kitakami expansions are delayed or cut, NAND oversupply destroys pricing despite AI demand, or realized capacity/utilization fails to improve AI-storage availability and economics versus the pre-announcement baseline.
title: AI infrastructure bottleneck expands from GPUs and power into persistent memory capacity
summary: Kioxia and Sandisk announced more than $31B of planned Japan investment through 2032 to expand advanced NAND flash supply, explicitly citing AI and data-driven demand. The event strengthens the thesis that AI infrastructure constraints are broadening beyond accelerators into storage/memory, but the investment is contingent on government support and does not yet prove future utilization or returns.
delta: Upgrade NAND/storage capacity from a secondary AI-infrastructure input to a strategic capacity variable. Preserve the distinction between announced investment, completed capacity, utilized capacity, and economically productive capacity.
firstOrderImpacts: stronger forward capital spending on advanced NAND manufacturing in Japan
potentially improved long-run flash-memory supply for AI and data-intensive workloads
greater strategic importance of U.S.-Japan semiconductor collaboration and industrial support
secondOrderImpacts: AI infrastructure analysis should track memory/storage constraints alongside GPUs, networking, power and cooling
large sovereign/industrial-policy support packages may increasingly shape where AI supply-chain capacity is built
if storage capacity lags accelerator deployment, data movement and persistence can become a hidden bottleneck in agentic and physical-AI systems

alphaHunter.hypothesis: Memory-capacity expansion signals will improve forecasts of AI infrastructure bottlenecks and storage pricing before those constraints are obvious in hyperscaler capex or GPU-demand headlines.
alphaHunter.baseline: GPU shipments, hyperscaler capex guidance and broad semiconductor indices
alphaHunter.alternativeData: NAND fab construction milestones, wafer starts, bit growth, equipment orders, Japanese subsidy approvals, enterprise SSD pricing, inventory days and AI-storage deployment announcements
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: lead time and forecast improvement for enterprise SSD/NAND pricing, AI storage shortages and infrastructure deployment delays versus the baseline
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill this alpha layer if memory-specific signals do not improve held-out forecasts of storage pricing, shortages or AI deployment bottlenecks beyond ordinary semiconductor and capex indicators.
